text:
lena: Follow-up on the packaging/upgrade RFC: thinking about chunk-level dedupe + GC strategy for big model shards in air-gapped installs. want to avoid storing multiple full copies during rollouts.
omar: yup. the naive `download-then-swap` wastes disk. proposal: stream into a content-addressed store and activate by writing an activation marker that points at manifest-level roots.
rachel: how do we handle partial transfers and interrupted rollouts? operators get anxious when nodes show 80% disk used by half-applied bundles.
lena: two parts: 1) transfer layer writes chunks by sha256 into /var/lib/redwood/blobs/<sha>.partial and finalizes with atomic rename to .blob once checksum verified. 2) activation is an atomic metadata update that references blobs by hash; no copying required.
ben: sounds good. what's GC policy? if activation just moves pointers, old blobs may leak.
lena: GC plan: keep a per-node reference-count manifest. every activation increments refs for referenced blobs; deactivation/deploy prunes refs. GC runs as a low-priority sweep: collects blobs with refcount==0 and age > configurable TTL (default 24h).
omar: we need to signal long-running prepares so GC won't erroneously delete in-progress blobs. propose `prepare` creates a soft-lock entry tied to txn id; GC treats soft-locks as refs.
rachel: operator UX: how does operator know space is reserved when doing a canary 10% rollout? need a `reserve_bytes` hint so planner can avoid oversubscription.
ben: add a `reserve_hint` in prepare call. control-plane sums expected reserves per node and makes scheduling decisions. also expose `node_free_bytes` in /agent/status.
lena: security: all blob manifests must be signed and include canonical ordering of chunk hashes so an attacker can't reorder. verification happens before rename to .blob.
omar: what about in-place model patching (delta updates)? Deltas reduce transfer size but complicate GC and activation mapping. maybe support deltas later as diff-on-top-of-blob where patch artifacts are also content-addressed.
rachel: rollback and canary activation: we should support a staged activation window where commit is delayed until canary telemetry looks good. Activation marker has fields: `desired=true/false`, `applied_at`, `canary_pct`, `expiry_ts`.
ben: implement activator service that watches metrics (from console) and either advances commit from canary to full or triggers rollback. Keep activator out of control-plane so it can be run in air-gapped environments by customers.
lena: API sketch (agent):
```
POST /v1/apps/:app_id/prepare
  body: { txn_id, manifest_hash, reserve_hint, signed_manifest }
GET  /v1/apps/:app_id/txns/:txn_id
POST /v1/apps/:app_id/txns/:txn_id/activate
POST /v1/apps/:app_id/txns/:txn_id/abort
GET  /v1/agent/status -> { free_bytes, accepts_prepares, capacity_score }
POST /v1/blobs/:sha/chunk -> streaming chunk upload
```
omar: make all endpoints idempotent and safe to retry. include `If-None-Match` style ETag headers for manifest binds.
rachel: edge-case: node runs out of reserved disk during multi-txn parallel prepares. agent should enforce `max_staging_bytes` and either reject new prepares or evict oldest non-committed txn by policy (LRU / operator-annotated critical flag).
ben: also add a `staging_quota` per-node that operator can tune. default to 30% of free space or a hard cap.
lena: performance note: content-addressed blobs allow cross-node dedupe when operator brings same USB seed to multiple nodes. we should document an optional `rebroadcast` mode where node can serve requested chunks to peers (signed and rate-limited). useful for disconnected clusters.
omar: +1 but lock down with ACLs and sign checks; otherwise risk of unauthorized blob propagation.
ops-bot: infra-bot: opened tracking ticket #1091 "chunked-cas-gc-activator-prototype" assigned to @lena and @ben :eyes:
rachel: next steps: small PoC agent that implements chunk streaming + finalize rename, a GC worker, and an activator that respects `canary_pct`. measure disk overhead during a canary rollout for a 4-node cluster.
lena: I'll write the PoC plan and a follow-up RFC appendix showing state machine diagrams and a sample `activation.json` manifest.
ben: i'll prototype the refcount store using SQLite for durability and metrics hooks for Console.
omar: i'll work on the agent status + reserve_hint plumbing in the scheduler.
rachel: thanks all. try to keep the activation semantics simple: pointer swap, signed manifest, soft-locks for prepares, GC window. minimizes operator surprises :thumbsup:
